text:
### Observed differences

- The direct successors of A25 and A26 changed almost completely. In the earlier window, A25 was followed immediately by A27 in about 99 of 100 cases, and A26 was followed by A41 (about 37 in 100), A35 (about 34) or A36 (about 28). In the later window, A25 is followed by A35, A36 or A41 in roughly equal shares (about one third each) and almost never directly by A27 (about 1 in 200), while A26 leads directly to A30 in about 99 of 100 cases. [DIR025, DIR026]
- The exit of the A35/A36/A41 group changed accordingly: earlier, each of the three led to A30 in about 28–37 of 100 of its outgoing transitions; later, each leads to A27 in about 31–34 of 100 and almost never to A30. Within the group, the three activities still follow one another in no fixed order in both windows. [DIR035, DIR036, DIR041, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- Six pairwise order relations reversed, with each pair occurring together in all 200 traces of both windows: A26 came before A35, A36 and A41 in about 99–100 of 100 cases earlier and after them in about 99 of 100 later, and the same reversal holds between A27 and the three group members. Orders not involving the group were stable (A25 before A26, A25 before A27, A27 before A26, and the group before A30, in both windows). [REL008, REL009, REL010, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL001, REL002, REL006, REL015, REL016, REL017]
- Event distances shifted consistently: A27 moved from directly after A25 (99 of 100 at distance 1) to about four steps after it (about 93 of 100), and A30 moved from four to five steps after A26 (about 93 of 100) to directly after it (about 98 of 100). A25 and A35 were within five steps in 1 of 200 traces earlier versus 199 of 200 later (likewise A35 and A27); A26 with A35 or A36 fell from 200 of 200 to about 1 of 200; A35, A36 or A41 with A30 fell from 200 of 200 to 1–2 of 200. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG010, LAG011, LAG014, LAG017]
- By event position, A35, A36 and A41 each moved earlier, from a mean of about 0.58–0.59 to about 0.41 of the trace length, while A26 (about 0.53 to 0.62) and A27 (about 0.38 to 0.47) moved later; A25 and A30 kept their positions. [POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS001, POS004]
- Outside this re-routing, A15 and A16, present in every trace in both windows, repeat slightly more often: mean occurrences per trace rose from about 1.6 to about 1.7, and A16 returns to A15 in about 41 of 100 of its outgoing transitions versus about 36 earlier. Several optional activities show modest participation shifts in both directions, e.g. A08 up from about 7 to 13 in 100 traces and A23 up from about 47 to 56, versus A04 down from about 15 to 8, A24 down from about 54 to 46 and A18 down from about 28 to 21. [OCC015, OCC016, DIR016, OCC004, OCC008, OCC018, OCC022, OCC023]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block of three activities A35, A36, A41 was re-routed to a different place in the sequence: in the earlier window it ran between A26 and A30 (A26 fed into it, it exited to A30) while A25 passed directly to A27; in the later window it runs between A25 and A27 (A25 feeds into it, it exits to A27) while A26 passes directly to A30. All seven activities (A25, A26, A27, A30, A35, A36, A41) occur in every trace in both windows, so this is a reordering of mandatory activities, not paths being taken with different frequencies and not activities becoming optional, repeated or removed. [DIR025, DIR026, DIR035, DIR036, DIR041, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL012, REL013, REL014]

The change is shown directly and consistently: successor profiles at A25, A26 and all three group members flipped from near-deterministic old to near-deterministic new behaviour, six order relations reversed completely with full co-occurrence support and reference strength at the top of its scale, and the lag and position shifts match a three-step block moving as a unit while A25 and A30 stayed in place. A competing reading in which A25 and A26 merely swapped roles is not supported, because A25's position remained at about 0.35 of the trace while A26's moved later. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG010, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS007]

Limitations: the evidence establishes the re-routing as behaviour but cannot distinguish a relocation of the block from an equivalent redefinition of its entry and exit connections, and the internal order of A35, A36 and A41 remains unfixed in both windows, so no internal reordering is implied. Residual old connections persist at about 1 in 200 cases (for example A25 still occasionally followed by A27), so the new routing is near-universal but not complete. [DIR025, REL018, REL019, REL020]

Other differences: A15 and A16 repeat slightly more often in the later window. The participation shifts in optional activities (A08, A21, A23 up; A03, A04, A11, A12, A13, A18, A22, A24 down) rest on single occurrence indicators without relational corroboration; a balanced pattern of small shifts is also what finite samples produce, so they may be sampling variation or knock-on effects of the re-routing rather than independent changes, and the evidence cannot separate these. [OCC015, OCC016, DIR016, OCC003, OCC004, OCC008, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, OCC018, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023]
